cards.text: Before this, a prophet named Agabus tied up his own feet and hands with Paul's belt and said the Jews of Jerusalem would bind the owner of that belt (Acts 21:11). That's not a warning, friend, that's a LIVE DEMONSTRATION. Paul said he was ready to be bound and even to die for the name of the Lord Jesus (Acts 21:13), and now he and his group arrive in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Paul and his group walk into Jerusalem. How do the brothers there receive them?

answers.text: They welcome them joyfully
They keep them waiting outside
They ask them to leave the city

cards.text: The next day Paul goes in to see James, and all the elders are there. Paul greets them and goes through it one by one. Not the highlight reel, friend. The FULL season.

cards.question: What does Paul go through one by one for James and the elders?

answers.text: What God had done among the Gentiles through him
Every argument he had with people on the road
His plans for where he would travel next

cards.question: When James and the elders hear Paul's report, they glorify God.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then they say to Paul, "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law." That's good news, friend, but I can HEAR the next word coming, and it's BUT.

cards.question: The elders say these believers are under the impression that Paul teaches the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake ___.

answers.text: Moses
David
Abraham

cards.question: According to the rumor about Paul, he tells those Jews to keep circumcising their children.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The elders ask, "What then should we do?" These believers will certainly hear that Paul has come, so the elders have a plan, and it starts with four men who have taken a vow.

cards.question: What do the elders ask Paul to do with these four men who took a vow?

answers.text: Purify himself with them and pay their expenses
Send them out to preach among the Gentiles
Bring them all before the high priest

cards.question: The elders say their plan will show everyone there's no truth to the rumors and that Paul also lives in obedience to the ___.

answers.text: law
council
priests

cards.text: Those expenses are so the four men can have their heads shaved. Paul's picking up the tab for FOUR shaved heads, and I can't even find a coupon for a mustache trim.
Then the elders bring up the Gentile believers. They've already written to them with their decision about what to stay away from.

cards.question: Which of these is on the elders' list for the Gentile believers to abstain from?

answers.text: Food sacrificed to idols
Trading in the marketplace
Travel on the Sabbath

cards.text: So the next day, Paul takes the four men and purifies himself along with them. No arguing, no 'let me sleep on it.' He just does it.

cards.question: Then Paul enters the temple. What is he there to do?

answers.text: Give notice of when their purification would be complete
Teach the crowds there about the Lord Jesus
Meet with the high priest in private

cards.text: The seven days are almost over, and Paul is SO close to the finish line. Then some Jews from the province of Asia see him at the temple.

cards.question: What do the Jews from the province of Asia do when they see Paul at the temple?

answers.text: Stir up the whole crowd and seize him
Ask him to explain his teaching
Report him to James and the elders

cards.text: They cry out, "Men of Israel, help us!" They say this is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against their people, their law and this place.

cards.question: The Jews from Asia aren't done. What else do they accuse Paul of doing at the temple?

answers.text: Bringing Greeks into the temple
Taking money from the temple treasury
Speaking against the high priest

cards.text: Here's where that charge comes from. They had seen Trophimus the Ephesian, one of the men traveling with Paul (Acts 20:4), with him in the city.

cards.question: The Jews from Asia saw Paul bring Trophimus into the temple.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: They saw Trophimus with Paul in the city and assumed the rest. That's like seeing your coworker in the parking lot and telling the whole office they were sitting in the boss's chair.
And now the whole city is stirred up. People come rushing together from everywhere.

cards.question: With the whole city rushing in, what does the crowd do with Paul?

answers.text: Seize him and drag him out of the temple
Lock him inside the temple courts
Take him to the house of the high priest

cards.text: At once the gates are shut. While they're trying to kill Paul, the commander of the Roman regiment gets a report that all Jerusalem is in turmoil.

cards.question: What does the commander of the Roman regiment do when he gets the report?

answers.text: Runs down with soldiers and centurions
Waits for the crowd to calm down
Sends one messenger to find out more

cards.question: When the crowd sees the commander and the soldiers, they stop beating Paul.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The commander comes up, arrests Paul and orders him bound with not one chain, friend, but TWO.

cards.question: Once Paul is in chains, what does the commander want to know?

answers.text: Who he is and what he has done
Where he has been staying in the city
Who first brought him into the temple

cards.text: Some in the crowd shout one thing, and some shout another. It's a group chat where everybody replies at once and NOBODY read the question.

cards.question: The commander can't get at the truth because of the uproar. What does he order?

answers.text: That Paul be brought into the barracks
That the crowd decide what happens next
That Paul be let go outside the gate

cards.question: Paul reaches the steps, but he doesn't climb them on his own. Why do the soldiers have to carry him?

answers.text: Because of the violence of the mob
Because he refused to climb them
Because guards had blocked the steps

cards.text: The crowd that follows him keeps shouting, "Away with him!" And that's where we leave Paul for now, friend, because this story is a long way from over.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'The next day Paul goes in to see James, and all the elders are there.' / 'Paul greets them and goes through it one by one.' / 'Not the highlight reel, friend.' / 'The FULL season.' Only the opening card may run past two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: James appears here for the first time in the passage, and the card never says who he is. It needs a simple identification, such as a leader of the church in Jerusalem.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says 'he tells those Jews to keep circumcising their children.' The phrase 'those Jews' points back to card 7, which is no longer on screen. The question should name the group itself: the Jews who live among the Gentiles.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The joke "No arguing, no 'let me sleep on it.'" clashes with the text. Acts 21:26 says Paul did this 'the next day,' so he did, in a sense, sleep on it. The joke has to fit what the text says.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'So the next day, Paul takes the four men and purifies himself along with them.' / "No arguing, no 'let me sleep on it.'" / 'He just does it.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'People come rushing together from everywhere' goes beyond the text. Acts 21:30 says only 'the people rushed together.' The words 'from everywhere' should come out.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Seven of the stop's nine choice cards are multiple choice. There are two true or false cards and no fill in the blank, so multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. Some cards should change type.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
